metric: Count of newly connected modeled exterior approach points from the fixed middle Lot 1 origin.

favorableAssumptions.text: The 2026 map and 2020 ramp inventory are combined as a hypothetical planning exercise, not a reconstructed observed 2020 or 2026 network.
Historical ramp IDs are associated with the two mapped crossings by the reviewed plausible alignment, not authoritative asset-to-edge identification.

In favorable scenarios ONLY, all non-ramp conditions along the mapped paths, including known sidewalk/approach defects and unknown widths, slopes, crossings and coverage, are assumed addressed or otherwise usable outside this four-project budget. Their work and costs are not included or estimated. No such work is observed.

The optional north Building 9 vertical transfer AND its usable landings are assumed available only in its explicitly enabled scenario; doors, levels, operating status and actual step-free continuity are unverified. A3 does not enable the transfer or its landings.
Endpoints represent exterior approach areas on a schematic map, not confirmed accessible entrances. Each counts once with equal weight; no people, usage, business value or ROI weights are inferred.

historicalEstimate.scope: Four published curb-ramp replacement assemblies only.

publishedPriority: Unavailable because the ramp 404 priority is unresolved.
limitation: The southern 404/405 pair has no mapped connection to the fixed middle Lot 1 origin or its targets. Its costs remain in the denominator. Any comparison is structurally specific to this origin, target set and inferred placement, not evidence of campus-wide algorithm performance.
boundary: Historical cost inputs and conditional modeled exterior connections. No current access, complete-route price, observed benefit, compliance assessment, campus-wide comparison or human-study claim.
